column5: git's own optdepend, and the reason scripts/git-credentials.sh can store a PAT encrypted instead of in plaintext. Arch ships git-credential-libsecret INSIDE the git package (/usr/lib/git-core/), but not the library it links against - without this row the helper is present and non-functional. The other half, org.freedesktop.secrets, comes from kwallet, which Plasma already pulls in, so it is not listed here
binary and package are both `fd`; `fdfind` is the Debian name

the package is `7zip`; `p7zip` was dropped from extra and survives only as a provides/replaces on it. That distinction is load-bearing here: bootstrap.sh validates manifest names against `pacman -Slq`, which lists PACKAGE NAMES and not provides, so `p7zip` was classified missing and silently dropped from the transaction - a machine with no 7z at all. Manifest rows must always name a real package, never a provides
